guide.title: The Perfect Hong Kong Layover: 10 Hours in
guide.description:
A 10-hour layover at HKG isn’t a delay — it’s a free day in one of the world’s most
electric cities. With the Airport Express running every 10 minutes straight into the
heart of the city, you can be standing on the Star Ferry watching the skyline
before your seatmates have even landed at their  fi nal destination.

data.name: Central Star Ferry Pier
data.description: Star Ferry Pier, Man, Kwong St, Central, Hong Kong Central Star Ferry Pier serves as a vital transportation hub in Hong Kong, connecting Central with Tsim Sha Tsui across Victoria Harbour. The iconic ferries o ff er stunning views of the skyline and harbor, making it a popular spot for both locals and tourists. The pier itself features modern amenities, including waiting areas and ticket services. Established in the late 19th century, it has been a signi fi cant part of Hong Kong's maritime history, with its distinctive green and white ferries being emblematic of the city. Visitors often enjoy the picturesque scenery and vibrant atmosphere at the pier.

data.name: Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade
data.description: Tsim Sha Tsui East, Hong Kong Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade is a scenic waterfront stretch located in Hong Kong, known for its stunning views of Victoria Harbour and the iconic skyline. The promenade features a wide walkway ideal for leisurely strolls, outdoor events, and cultural displays. Visitors can enjoy a variety of sculptures and installations along the path, including the famous Avenue of Stars, which pays tribute to Hong Kong's  fi lm industry. The area is also a popular vantage point for the Symphony of Lights show, where buildings come alive with vibrant colors and music. This picturesque location is a must-visit for anyone looking to experience the beauty and energy of Hong Kong.

data.name: Victoria Peak (The Peak)
data.description: Victoria Peak, or The Peak, is one of Hong Kong's most famous landmarks, o ff ering breathtaking views of the city skyline and Victoria Harbour. Accessible via the Peak Tram, which has been in operation since 1888, visitors can enjoy a scenic ride to the top. The Peak o ff ers a variety of dining and shopping options, along with the Sky Terrace 428, which provides the highest viewing platform in Hong Kong. Surrounded by lush greenery and walking trails, The Peak is an ideal spot for leisurely strolls while soaking in the natural beauty and impressive urban landscape.
data.address: 118 Peak Rd, The Peak, Hong Kong

data.name: Hong Kong Observation Wheel
data.description: The Hong Kong Observation Wheel is an iconic landmark situated in Central, o ff ering breathtaking views of the skyline and the vibrant Victoria Harbour. Standing at 60 meters tall, this Ferris wheel features climate-controlled cabins that allow visitors to enjoy a comfortable ride. Each rotation provides a panoramic perspective of the city's impressive architecture and waterfront. The surrounding area often hosts events and family-friendly activities, enhancing the experience for tourists and locals alike. Tim Ho Wan (Sham Shui Po) Dim Sum 9-11 Fuk Wing Street, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China +852 2788 1226 Tim Ho Wan, located in Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong, is famous for its a ff ordable Michelin-starred dim sum. Founded by former chefs from a prestigious hotel, it o ff ers a variety of traditional Cantonese dim sum dishes. The restaurant is particularly known for its baked BBQ pork buns, which have become a signature item. Despite its humble setting, Tim Ho Wan has attracted food enthusiasts from around the world, eager to experience its high-quality yet reasonably priced o ff erings.
